title: OAuth provider configuration registry v1
description: The preconfigured provider-capability record that docs/architecture/AUTHORITATIVE_STATE_AND_PLATFORM_CONTRACT.md and docs/decisions/ADR-015-SESSION_AUTHENTICATION.md both name as the thing an OAuth transaction binds, and that existed in neither as data. ADR-015 makes RFC 9207 issuer validation the control that closes the mix-up attack and says a response arriving without an iss for a provider recorded as supporting it is a failure; the contract document says a provider without RFC 9207 support is bound by its stored transaction provider and its unique provider-specific redirect path instead. Both rules are conditional on a capability record, so until this file existed neither rule could be evaluated and the asymmetry between the two callback operations in packages/schemas/openapi-v1.yaml rested on nothing. Every value here is server-held configuration: no field in this file is ever selected, echoed or influenced by a callback parameter, which is the confused-deputy rule the contract document states. docs/security/AUTHENTICATION_AND_RECOVERY.md is the normative owner.

claim_scope.description: What a reader may conclude from this file. It is required rather than optional because every endpoint, scope and capability below is transcribed configuration rather than an observation: nothing in this repository has performed an authorization request against either provider. A record whose verification state is unverified is a statement of intent, and the scope line is where that is said once rather than implied by omission.

capability.description: A provider capability the protocol's behaviour depends on. `supported` and `unsupported` are observations and require a primary source and the date it was read; `unverified` is the absence of an observation and requires the work unit that will make one. An unverified capability may never be relied on as a control: scripts/repository/validate_oauth_identity_contract.py refuses a registry that claims a capability while its provider's verification state records that nothing was observed.

verification_owner.description: The work unit in docs/implementation/PR_SIZED_WORK_BREAKDOWN.md that will observe this capability against a live provider.

provider_id.description: The spelling every other artifact uses for this provider: the CHECK literal on linked_identities.provider and oauth_transactions.provider, and the enum member on Identity.provider. One spelling across the four owners is D-079's rule; a second spelling here would be a provider the rest of the system cannot name.

issuer.description: The immutable issuer the transaction records at creation. A callback never selects it.

client_id_reference.description: Where the deployment reads the client identifier from. The identifier itself is environment configuration and is never committed: a literal here would be one string that must differ between the local build and production, so the file would be wrong in at least one of them by construction.

redirect_uri.description: The exact redirect URI registered with the provider. Exact means byte-equal: no prefix rule, no wildcard and no path suffix, because a redirect matched by prefix is the redirection attack the exactness exists to refuse.

start_path.description: The OpenAPI path that begins this provider's transaction. Checked against packages/schemas/openapi-v1.yaml rather than trusted.

callback_path.description: The OpenAPI path this provider's authorization response returns to. It is provider-specific by design: the contract document makes the unique provider-specific redirect path the binding that replaces RFC 9207 for a provider without it, so two providers sharing one callback path would remove the only mix-up control the launch configuration actually has.

pkce_method.description: S256 only. `plain` is admitted by RFC 7636 and is not admitted here: it makes the challenge equal to the verifier, so an attacker who observes the authorization request holds the verifier.

device_flow.description: Whether this provider offers RFC 8628 device authorization. It gates which providers /auth/device/start may name; ADR-015 restricts the device path to registered limited-input profiles and forbids unattended polling.

scopes.description: The minimum scope set requested for sign-in and linking. An empty list is admissible and means the default read-only grant; it is not a placeholder for 'not decided yet', which is what the verification state records.

verification.description: Whether anything in this row has been observed against the live provider. `unverified` is the honest launch state and is not a defect; claiming a capability while it holds is.

revision.description: Monotonic per provider. An OAuth transaction records the revision it was created under, so a configuration change cannot retroactively change what an in-flight transaction agreed to.

review_due_at.description: When this row stops being a current statement about the provider. It is a bounded warranty rather than a wall-clock expiry: the validator checks it is later than recorded_at and no more than 365 days after it, so a row cannot be written with a warranty nobody will ever be asked to renew.
